stories.headline: Houthi missile strike on Riyadh airport kills 12 and injures hundreds
stories.body:
Houthi forces struck King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with a missile on Saturday. At least 12 people died in the attack. Over 300 people suffered injuries at the airport. Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation reported that 309 people were injured. The aviation authority said some of the injured are in critical condition.

Four Saudi citizens and two Bangladeshis died in the strike. Citizens from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine, and Sudan were also killed. An unnamed regional official said a missile hit a terminal complex. The complex houses terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights. Regional officials said earlier Houthi attacks on the airport on Thursday damaged three planes.

Flight operations at the Riyadh airport were temporarily stopped after the attack. Planes flying to Riyadh were sent to other airports. FlightAware reported that at least 225 flights were cancelled over 24 hours. The US and UK embassies in Riyadh warned their citizens to stay away. They told citizens to avoid the airport and the surrounding area.

Another strike occurred in eastern Saudi Arabia. A military coalition fighting the Houthis said a projectile fell near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.

The Houthis warned airline companies to stop flying in Saudi airspace. They said any plane in Saudi airspace except over Mecca and Medina is a target. The Houthis also warned Pakistan against fighting them for Saudi Arabia. They said they would treat Pakistan like Saudi Arabia if Pakistan gets involved.

US President Donald Trump spoke to reporters at the White House. Reporters asked if the United States would join strikes against the Houthis. Trump said he will make a decision soon. Regional officials told the AP last month that Saudi Arabia was running low on missile interceptors. Saudi Arabia asked France, Britain, Pakistan, and Egypt for air defense help.

Earlier strikes hit King Khalid International Airport and Abha International Airport on October 6 and 7. The aviation authority said those earlier attacks killed three people. Those attacks also injured 36 people.

In Yemen, pro-government forces secured the port of Mokha. Mokha sits on the Bab al-Mandab Strait near the Red Sea. Spokesman Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili gave details about the fighting. He said government forces killed at least 1,150 Houthis in operation 'Dawn of Yemen'. Forces completed almost 2,000 targeted operations during that mission.

claims.text: At least 12 people were killed and over 300 injured after a missile struck King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday, according to Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA).
GACA reported that 309 people were injured in the Riyadh airport attack, with some in critical condition.
The fatalities at King Khalid International Airport included four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, and one citizen each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine, and Sudan.
A regional official speaking on condition of anonymity said a missile struck a complex housing terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights at King Khalid International Airport.
Regional officials said Houthi attacks on the Riyadh airport on Thursday damaged three planes.
Operations at King Khalid International Airport were temporarily suspended following the attack, and flights bound for Riyadh were diverted to other destinations.
At least 225 flights at King Khalid International Airport were cancelled over the 24 hours preceding the report, according to FlightAware.
The US and UK embassies in Riyadh advised their citizens to avoid King Khalid International Airport and surrounding areas following the incident.
A projectile fell near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam in eastern Saudi Arabia, according to the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis.
The Houthis warned aviation companies to avoid using Saudi airspace, stating that any aircraft operating there except over Mecca and Medina is a target.
The Houthis stated that if Pakistan engages in military activities against them on behalf of Saudi Arabia, Pakistan will be treated in the same fashion as Saudi Arabia.
When asked if the US would join strikes against the Houthis, US President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House that he will make a decision soon.
Regional officials told the AP last month that Saudi Arabia was running low on missile interceptors and requested air defense support from France, Britain, Pakistan, and Egypt.
Earlier attacks targeting King Khalid International Airport and Abha International Airport on October 6 and 7 resulted in three deaths and 36 injuries, according to GACA.
Yemeni pro-government forces secured the port of Mokha on the Bab al-Mandab Strait at the southern end of the Red Sea.
Spokesman Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili said Yemeni government forces killed at least 1,150 Houthis in almost 2,000 targeted operations under operation 'Dawn of Yemen'.

stories.headline: Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia kills 20 as Trump demands new leadership in Ukraine
stories.body:
Russian forces attacked the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia with five glide bombs on Saturday. The attack killed at least 20 people, including four children. At least 32 other people were injured in the bombing.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke about the attack. He said Russia was saying thanks for a US deal easing sanctions on Russian diesel exports. US President Donald Trump said Russia agreed to supply over 300,000 tonnes of diesel right away. Russia will supply 500,000 tonnes in November and millions more later.

Trump said Ukraine needs a new leader who can make a deal. He said Zelensky has not done enough to end the war. Trump claimed Ukraine lost 30 percent of its land and 2 million people under Zelensky. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga defended Zelensky. Sybiga said Zelensky has the support of the Ukrainian people.

In other attacks, a Russian missile hit a restaurant in Kyiv and wounded seven people. Russia said its drones struck a Kyiv data center and a ship carrying military supplies. Ukrainian attacks killed four civilians in Russian-occupied Luhansk.

claims.text: Russia attacked the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia with five glide bombs, killing at least 20 people including four children and injuring at least 32 others.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attacks on Zaporizhzhia were Russia expressing 'its thanks' for a deal announced by US President Donald Trump easing sanctions on Russian diesel exports.

Donald Trump stated that Russia agreed to immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel, 500,000 tonnes in November, 1 million tonnes immediately thereafter, and an additional 3 million tonnes shortly after.
US President Donald Trump stated that Ukraine needs 'a new leader who can make a deal' and suggested Volodymyr Zelensky has not done enough to end the war.
US President Donald Trump claimed that under President Zelensky, Ukraine has lost 30 percent of its country and had over 2 million people killed.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga defended President Zelensky, stating that Zelensky has the support of the Ukrainian people and is doing his job well.
A Russian missile attack on Saturday afternoon hit a restaurant in Kyiv, wounding seven people.
Russia's Defence Ministry said its drones struck a data-processing centre in Kyiv and a cargo ship carrying military supplies to the port of Odesa.
Ukrainian attacks in the Russian-occupied Luhansk region killed four civilians and wounded five over a 24-hour period, according to Russian-installed governor Leonid Pasechnik.

vocab.meaning: penalties imposed on a country to limit its trade

stories.headline: Hurricane Isaias weakens after killing four people and causing power outages
stories.body:
Hurricane Isaias made landfall on Florida's panhandle as a category 2 storm late Friday. It weakened to a post-tropical cyclone on Saturday. The storm produced winds of 105 mph.

At least four people died during the storm. Two deaths occurred in Escambia County, Florida, and two in Alabama. Trees fell on homes and killed two people. One person in Escambia County died from generator gas poisoning. Four family members went to the hospital.

Nearly 550,000 customers had no power across Florida, Alabama, and Georgia on Saturday afternoon. Outages peaked earlier at over 900,000. The storm blew off a hotel roof in Pensacola and flattened a boathouse in Destin. It also damaged a high-rise building in Panama City Beach.

US President Donald Trump approved emergency help for Florida, Alabama, and Georgia. The US Department of Energy released 4 million barrels of crude oil due to supply disruptions.

claims.text: Isaias made landfall late Friday on Florida's panhandle as a category 2 hurricane before weakening to a post-tropical cyclone on Saturday.
Isaias produced maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (169 km/h).
At least four people died during Isaias, including two in Escambia County, Florida, and two in Alabama.
One death in Escambia County, Florida, and one in Birmingham, Alabama, occurred when trees fell on homes during the storm.
A person in Escambia County, Florida, died from carbon monoxide poisoning after running a generator in a closed garage, and four family members were hospitalized.
Nearly 550,000 customers were without power across Florida, Alabama, and Georgia on Saturday afternoon, down from a peak of over 900,000.
Isaias caused structural damage including blowing the roof off a Pensacola hotel, flattening a boathouse in Destin, and damaging a high-rise facade in Panama City Beach.
Donald Trump authorized FEMA to provide resources to Georgia and previously approved emergency declarations for Florida and Alabama.
The US Department of Energy authorized an emergency exchange of up to 4 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve due to supply disruptions caused by Hurricane Isaias.

vocab.meaning: the arrival of a storm over land
disturbances that stop a process or event

stories.headline: Delhi Police detain thousands to stop anti-CEC protest
stories.body:
Delhi Police conducted large-scale detentions on October 10 to stop a youth protest. Protesters demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over deleted voter lists. Police enforced Section 163 prohibitory orders in New Delhi district. Senior police officers said nearly 3,000 people were detained across Delhi.

Authorities closed gates at 45 Delhi Metro stations. They cancelled more than 250 trains. Officials suspended mobile internet in central Delhi. Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan approved internet cuts near eight temporary jail sites. The Delhi government converted four sports stadiums into temporary jails. The Supreme Court said on Friday that authorities cannot use a sledgehammer to kill a fly.

Police detained several political leaders. AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal was detained while leaving his house. Former Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee was detained at a bus stop with several lawmakers. Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan and former Tripura chief minister Manik Sarkar were also detained.

Officers detained CJP representatives Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, and Ashutosh Ranka after they boarded a flight. Police detained YouTuber Dhruv Rathee at a flat in Gurugram. Advocate Nipun Saxena said detaining CJP members outside order zones was illegal. Former Supreme Court judge Abhay S. Oka said authorities must give reasons for restraint quickly.

BJP leaders strongly criticized the protest. BJP president Nitin Nabin alleged two groups worked with foreign forces to hurt India. BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra called the protest a flop show. Patra called Congress leader Rahul Gandhi Mir Jafar. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta accused Gandhi and Kejriwal of creating trouble.

Congress supported the youth but did not join the street protests. Rahul Gandhi spoke at an event in Chennai. He praised the students and called top officials villains.

claims.text: Delhi Police conducted large-scale detentions on October 10, 2026, to stop a youth protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over electoral roll deletions.
Prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were in force in Delhi's New Delhi district during the protest.
Nearly 3,000 people were detained across Delhi during Saturday's protest, according to senior police officers.
Authorities closed entry and exit gates at 45 Delhi Metro stations, cancelled over 250 trains, and suspended central Delhi internet services due to the protest.
Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan approved mobile internet suspension within 500 metres of eight temporary jail sites in Delhi from noon to 10pm on October 10.
The Delhi government notified sites including Chhatrasal Stadium, Rajiv Gandhi Stadium, Yamuna Sports Complex, and Surajmal Stadium as temporary jails.
The Supreme Court observed on Friday that authorities cannot use a sledgehammer to kill a fly regarding the scale of public transport restrictions in Delhi.
AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal was detained as he attempted to leave his residence for the protest.
Former Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee staged a sit-in at a South Avenue bus stop before being detained alongside several Trinamool Congress MPs.
Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan and former Tripura chief minister Manik Sarkar were among those detained in Delhi.
CJP representatives Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police after boarding their Air India flight upon arrival in Delhi.
YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was detained at a residential flat in Gurugram.
Advocate Nipun Saxena stated that detaining CJP representatives from areas in Delhi-NCR where prohibitory orders were not in force was wholly illegal.
Former Supreme Court judge Abhay S. Oka noted that Article 22 of the Constitution obligates authorities to communicate grounds for restraint as soon as possible.
BJP president Nitin Nabin alleged that two anarchic groups, one from the INDIA bloc and another led by Arvind Kejriwal and CJP, were colluding with foreign forces to destabilise India.
BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra described the Delhi protest as a flop show by anarchist forces and called Rahul Gandhi Mir Jafar.
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta accused Rahul Gandhi and Arvind Kejriwal of using CJP as their B-team to turn Delhi into a political battleground.
Congress kept away from Saturday's protests in Delhi but voiced support for the agitating youth.
Rahul Gandhi spoke at the sixth edition of his youth outreach programme, Chhatron Ki Goonj, at Island Grounds in Chennai.
Rahul Gandhi praised protesting students and accused Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Mohan Bhagwat, Gyanesh Kumar, and Ajit Doval of being the villains of the story.

vocab.meaning: used to forbid or stop certain actions
held in official custody or prevented from leaving

stories.headline: Fresh ethnic violence in Manipur leaves nine people dead
stories.body:
Clashes and village attacks killed at least five people in Manipur's Kamjong and Ukhrul districts. The violence started on Friday evening. Former Manipur Chief Minister Nongthombam Biren Singh said seven people died in 24 hours. Scroll.in reported that nine people died between Friday and Saturday.

A 42-year-old Kuki woman named Domkhonei Touthang was shot dead in Chassad Kuki village. The Kuki Students' Organisation blamed security forces for her death. Gunfights killed a 22-year-old man named Michael Ngamminlen Haokip on Saturday morning. A 40-year-old Gurkha farmer named Sandeep Rai was shot dead while driving.

Attackers burned at least 14 homes in Kamjong district. Around Chassad, 10 houses and 20 shops burned down. The Tangkhul Naga Long committee alleged Kuki extremists killed two Naga civilians. Four Naga volunteers died in separate attacks. One guard was reportedly beheaded in a video.

Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Delhi. District officials imposed emergency movement restrictions in parts of Kamjong district.

claims.text: At least five people were killed in clashes and village attacks in Manipur's Kamjong and Ukhrul districts starting Friday evening, October 9, 2026.
Former Manipur Chief Minister Nongthombam Biren Singh stated that seven people died in violent incidents across Manipur within 24 hours.
Nine persons were killed between Friday and Saturday across Manipur's Kamjong, Kangpokpi, and Ukhrul districts.
A 42-year-old Kuki woman named Domkhonei Touthang was shot dead in Chassad Kuki village in Kamjong district on Friday night.
The Kuki Students' Organisation alleged that Indian Reserve Battalion personnel opened fire on unarmed women in Chassad village, killing Domkhonei Touthang.
A 22-year-old man named Michael Ngamminlen Haokip was killed during continuing gunfights in Kamjong district on Saturday morning.
A 40-year-old Gurkha farmer, Sandeep Rai, was shot dead while driving on the Mahadev-Talui road in Ukhrul district on Saturday.
At least 14 homes belonging to members of the Kuki and Naga communities were set on fire during the violence in Kamjong.
At least 10 houses and 20 shops were burned down in and around Chassad in Kamjong district on Saturday.
The Working Committee of the Tangkhul Naga Long alleged that Kuki extremists set fire to nine houses and killed two Naga civilians in Ningchou village.
Four Naga village volunteers were killed in separate attacks along the Imphal-Tamenglong road and in Makui, Kangpokpi district.
Three Naga village guards were killed in Makui, Kangpokpi district, with one guard, Ajinpou Ringkangmai, allegedly beheaded in a video circulated on social media.
Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Saturday to discuss peace efforts.
Kamjong District Magistrate L. N. Kashung imposed Section 163 BNSS prohibitory orders within a 400-metre radius of Chassad Police Gate Junction.

vocab.meaning: people who hold radical opinions and may use violence
